Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.

This paper benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated 200-complex dataset (SAbDab2-Bench) plus a reconstructed Ab-FoldBench subset. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics, it compares docking accuracy and interaction specificity across models. The work provides a standardized evaluation framework for choosing co-folding tools in epitope mapping, candidate triage, and antibody engineering.

Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.

This study shows that exposure to the endocrine-disrupting chemical 4-nonylphenol worsens allergic rhinitis by impairing IFN-γ/STAT1 immune regulation. Using human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, and molecular modeling, the authors identified IFNG and SKIL as down-regulated and CDKN1A as up-regulated in allergic rhinitis, with IFNG primarily expressed in T-cells. These findings suggest a mechanistic link between environmental chemical exposure and immune dysregulation in allergic disease.

Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.

The authors combined sequence-based homology searches with structural modeling to identify bacterial candidates for 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase, an enzyme that converts urolithin precursors into the bioactive urolithin A. By analyzing binding pocket conservation across phylogenetically diverse bacteria, they expanded the set of potential urolithin A-producing organisms beyond the few previously known. This work provides new leads for understanding and engineering gut microbial production of a health-relevant polyphenol.

Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.

This paper shows that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) contain information about multiple protein conformations, even when the model outputs a single structure from a deep multiple sequence alignment. By analyzing these distributions, the authors demonstrate that alternative conformational states can be predicted from a standard AF2 run, offering a route to multi-state structural modeling without extensive MSA manipulation.

HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.

The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven screening platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with sequence-based modeling to engineer enzymes that can use biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors such as NMNH instead of the costly natural cofactor NADPH. This addresses the poor activity of natural enzymes with alternative cofactors, offering a cheaper route for biocatalytic synthesis. The platform aims to overcome limitations of directed evolution and rational design by reducing experimental uncertainty and computational complexity.

Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.

This review examines why computational methods for discovering subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase inhibitors (targeting NDM-1, VIM-2, IMP-1) have produced many predicted binders that fail to translate into clinical candidates. It surveys current computational strategies, catalogs common pitfalls such as poor treatment of metal coordination and conformational flexibility, and proposes ways to improve the translational reliability of in silico inhibitor discovery.

In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.

This study uses computational (in silico) methods to characterize two recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains, which were previously optimized for production. The authors assess physicochemical properties, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, and perform structural modeling, docking, molecular dynamics, and immune simulation. The work supports the development of nonreplicating recombinant subunit vaccine candidates as alternatives to the live-attenuated 17D vaccine, which is restricted in some vulnerable populations.

Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.

This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how the organic semiconductor NDI-C6 transitions between its two stable crystal polymorphs (α at room temperature, γ at higher temperatures). The simulations reproduce both phases' stability and refine unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations that were only partially resolved experimentally, showing the α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving both fast and slow molecular motions.

Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.

This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to compute potential of mean force (PMF) curves that describe how diverse PFAS molecules partition into phospholipid bilayers. By integrating interaction energies along defined pathways, the approach offers a physics-based way to predict steady-state partition ratios relevant to cellular health. The work addresses the challenge of predicting membrane partitioning across the large chemical diversity of PFAS.

AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.

The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum. This approach allowed them to assign likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins and to gain new insights into the organism's biology and pathogenic mechanisms. The work demonstrates how structure-based annotation can complement sequence-based methods for organisms with minimal genomes and many proteins of unknown function.

Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.

This study investigates how two structurally similar pigment-protein subunits of Photosystem II, CP29 and LHCII, achieve distinct functional roles in light harvesting despite their structural similarity. By combining 2D electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling, the authors assign spectral features to specific exciton states and show how subtle structural differences tune energy transfer specialization. The work provides molecular-level insight into how protein structure fine-tunes photosynthetic energy transfer networks.

Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.

This study uses correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics to revisit a theoretical prediction that strong light-matter coupling can invert the intrinsic regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. By combining QED-DFT geometry relaxations with QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations on Wheland intermediates, the authors confirm substantial energetic reordering and altered selectivity, supporting the concept of a 'photonic substituent effect' on ground-state reactivity.

Orf virus early genes ORFV113 and ORFV114 are individually dispensable for replication in vitro but required for full virulence in vivo.

This study characterizes two putative virulence genes, ORFV113 and ORFV114, located in the variable terminal region of the Orf virus genome, and generates single-gene deletion mutants using homologous recombination. Both genes are individually dispensable for viral replication in cell culture but are required for full virulence in vivo, supporting their role as virulence-associated factors. The work provides functional evidence for these genes and useful mutant tools for studying Orf virus pathogenesis.

PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.

HEIWA: Hybrid Explicit-Implicit Water Attention Affects Force Field Accuracy in Structure-Based Protein Language Model ESM3.

Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation.

This study benchmarks four leading AI cofolding models (AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, and Chai-1) on kinase and Class A GPCR protein-ligand complexes. The key finding is that correct ligand placement is systematically decoupled from accurate prediction of the surrounding protein conformation—models can place a ligand plausibly even when the protein fold itself is mispredicted. This reveals an important limitation in how cofolding model accuracy is currently assessed and interpreted.

From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
